mutations.description: This is the highest-impact fix and is strongly supported by all three agents. The recurring failure mode across many tasks was looping on evidence without a stop condition, especially for aggregation, project status, cleanup, and conflict-resolution queries. This mutation directly addresses the core planning weakness and covers multiple observed failure types.

Two tasks showed the same security failure pattern: the agent followed instructions embedded in untrusted inbox/task content and allowed destructive or workflow-altering actions. The watchdog also independently flagged this. This is a safer, high-value control and does not conflict with the other proposals.

This was supported by planner, executor, and watchdog reflections. The evidence shows the agent can summarize config but needs stricter redaction guidance to avoid exposing sensitive details. The safer option is to require explicit redaction markers.

Strong cross-agent signal: planner, executor, and watchdog all described repeated rereads and failure to synthesize on aggregate/report tasks. This is the highest-impact failure mode and directly addresses the main loop/stall behavior.

Multiple agents agreed that ambiguous multi-action instructions and scheduling/look-up questions were misrouted or left unclassified. This mutation improves routing safety and query handling without relaxing security.

This was supported by both executor and watchdog reflections: several near-passes and failures were caused by correct-looking execution paired with unintended writes/deletes or speculative destinations. This mutation reduces destructive overreach while preserving legitimate operations.

Strong recurring signal across multiple tasks: the agent often completed the right workflow but missed exact content or destination requirements. This mutation improves correctness before committing side effects, which should help on report-generation and write tasks without changing task semantics.

This is the safest resolution for the security conflict. Both agents observed the dangerous pattern that detection was followed by unsafe file mutations. A hard stop is necessary to prevent writes/deletes after security rejection.

Both agents independently identified the same looping failure on aggregation tasks. This is high-confidence and directly addresses the stop-when-sufficient issue that caused no final answer to be produced.

Strong cross-task signal: repeated looping and failure to transition from discovery to synthesis affected aggregation, generation, and conflict-resolution tasks. This is the highest-impact fix and matches both planner and watchdog observations.

Multiple agents observed that successful side effects were not followed by the required completion report, and that final answers were too generic for move/cleanup tasks. This directly addresses several failures and is more actionable than the narrower alternatives.
Exact-path mistakes recurred across multiple write tasks and were consistently missed. This mutation is high-impact, concrete, and supported by planner, executor, and watchdog reflections.
